entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call may be recorded for quality assurance. Please say 'Technical Support' or 'Customer Service'.
Connecting you to the next available agent.
Thank you for calling VeloFit, my name is Sarah. How can I help you today?
I need to return a VeloBand Pulse.
Okay, I can look into that for you. To get started, could I have your name and order number?

Thank you, Mark. Pulling that up now... Okay, I see the VeloBand Pulse delivered on December 15th. To make sure I understand correctly, what specifically is the issue? Is it a technical fault or more of a preference?
It doesn't matter. I just don't need it. I just want to return it. Yes or no, can you process the return?
I understand you're looking for a direct answer. Based on the delivery date of December 15th, I'm afraid it is now too late to start a return for this item.
Too late? I just got it a few weeks ago for Christmas. What are you talking about?
I can definitely clarify that. Our return policy for the VeloBand Pulse is ten days from the date of receipt. Since this device was delivered 23 days ago, it's outside that window.
Ten days? That's insane. Why is the policy so short for this specific product?

I understand the surprise, and I apologize for the frustration. The reason for the strict policy is that the VeloBand Pulse is a wearable device that has direct skin contact. For health, hygiene, and sanitation reasons, we cannot accept them back after that initial 10-day period.
So because of a hygiene rule I'm just stuck with it? That seems like a convenient excuse.

I'm sorry you feel that way, but the policy is firm for the health and safety of all our customers. I am unable to process a return or offer credit for this order. The system will not allow me to override it.
Fine. This was a complete waste of my time. Goodbye.
I understand. Thank you for calling VeloFit. Have a good day.
